name: Grove in Bloom
award: 2024 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Pedcor Investments plans Grove in Bloom, a 264-unit, all income-restricted family apartment community (eleven three-story buildings) for households at 30% to 80% AMI in the Bloom master-planned community in east Fort Collins. It won 2024 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA, with up to $64,992,920 of CHFA private activity bonds.
why_it_matters: It is one of the largest 4% deals in the round and pairs dollar-for-dollar tax-exempt bonds with a HUD 221(d)(4) loan, with a Housing Catalyst partnership supplying the property tax exemption; the city reported its Bloom filing under construction in April 2026, but no bond closing record was found.

status.label: Credits awarded; Bloom Filing 3 reported under construction (April 2026); bond closing not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA reserved the credits in November 2024 and held a TEFRA hearing on the bonds on 2025-09-10. The City of Fort Collins' Bloom page says in an April 2026 update that Bloom Filing 3 (the 360-apartment filing that contains this project) is under construction and that 264 of its units are planned as affordable housing. No public bond closing or building permit record specific to Grove in Bloom was found; the application had targeted a June 2025 financial closing.

next_step: Watch for a CHFA bond closing, a HUD 221(d)(4) firm commitment, and Fort Collins building permits or a final development plan record for Bloom Filing 3.

facts.value: North and west of E. Mulberry Street and Greenfield Court, southeast of the southern terminus of Delozier Road, Fort Collins 80524, in the Bloom community (Mulberry PUD)

Bloom Filing 3 Multi-Family Dwellings, PDP220011: 15 three-story, 24-unit buildings (360 apartments) on 16.36 acres zoned LMN and MMN, approved by the Planning and Zoning Commission on 2023-12-21. At least 264 of the 360 units are to be LIHTC affordable; the 2023 CHFA application says the other 96 units are a separate development at 80% AMI and market rate. Grove in Bloom's eleven buildings are inferred to be part of this filing.
Eleven three-story, 24-unit garden buildings, wood frame on concrete foundations with pitched asphalt shingle roofs, fiber cement and masonry exteriors; clubhouse, pool, playground, dog park
All-electric with rooftop solar estimated at 600 kW (cut from 1,485 kW in the earlier application to reduce cost)
Pedcor Investments-2023-CLXXXVI, L.P. (an Indiana limited partnership) or another Pedcor affiliate
Housing Catalyst (the Fort Collins housing authority) is to be a partner, providing a property tax exemption
Bus stop about 0.3 to 0.6 mile away; the sponsor will run a resident shuttle to a downtown bus stop and a shopping center
The 2024 application says the tract lost its Qualified Census Tract status in 2024; the 2023 application described it as a QCT

background.text: The Mulberry PUD master plan (ODP210002), about 1,600 homes on 226 acres now branded Bloom, was approved by Fort Collins City Council on 2021-12-16.

Pedcor took part in the master developer's subdivision process and says it negotiated higher-density three-story buildings and cost-efficient design standards. Site costs are higher than typical but are offset dollar-for-dollar by a lower land cost, per the applicant; the land price is not public.

In 2023 Round Two the same 264-unit plan offered 41 units at 30% AMI and the rest at 50% to 70% AMI, with $58,285,000 of bonds, $4,796,901 federal and $1,100,000 state credit requested. After feedback that 15% at 30% AMI was high for its size, the 2024 version cut 30% AMI units to 14 and added 40% and 80% AMI bands.

The market study cited a 1.5% overall multifamily vacancy rate and 0.7% for comparable affordable properties, with four of five affordable properties in the market area keeping waitlists (one up to 111 households). Its main weakness was a low walk score.
The Phase I found no environmental issues. A neighborhood meeting was held for the master plan with no opposition to this site, per the applicant.
The applicant says Pedcor has developed five 4% credit deals in Colorado in the past 10 years and manages a national portfolio of over 25,000 affordable units.

discrepancies.text: The award report gives $4,730,725 of federal credit and $1,714,655 of state credit, while the applicant report lists $4,280,300 federal and $1,705,822 state requested.
CHFA's award description names the health screening partner as the Health District of Northern Larimer County, while the application calls it the Health District of Northern Colorado.
The 2022 city filing narrative says the affordable units will serve households at or below 60% AMI, while the CHFA award includes 57 units at 70% and 80% AMI under income averaging.
